answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: score identities on graph independence, not headcount, because sparrow only stays cheap while a clique of fresh wallets answers only each other and its independence score collapses. Concretely, copper is enforced in the ledger: Sanctions are per-cluster, so one detection retires an entire fleet instead of one wallet. Any wharf approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
